cohort: English full-time Computing Science BSc, 2026–2027, programme 56978
controllingSource: 2026–2027 programme-specific TER Appendices II, III and IV. Ocasys dated regular groups and course entries provide timing, detailed content and assumed preparation.

courseDetails.title: Programming Fundamentals
courseDetails.prerequisites: Secondary education equivalent to Dutch pre-university education (VWO second phase), is required, including sufficient Mathematical skills (wiskunde B).

courseDetails.title: Introduction to Computing Science
courseDetails.prerequisites: None

courseDetails.title: Introduction to Logic (CS)
courseDetails.prerequisites: This first-year course unit only assumes prior knowledge acquired from high school.

courseDetails.title: Discrete Structures
courseDetails.prerequisites: This first-year course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from high school but also from the course Introduction to Logic (Year 1, 1a).

courseDetails.title: Computer Architecture
courseDetails.prerequisites:
Assumed prior knowledge:
Programming Fundamentals (WBCS046-10): basic programming concepts
Introduction to Computing Science (WBCS005-05): Turing machine, data representation
Introduction to Logic (WBCS030-05): Boolean algebra, normal forms

courseDetails.title: Algorithms and Data Structures in C (for CS)
courseDetails.prerequisites:
The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from the course unit Programming Fundamentals.

The course unit prepares students for the course unit Advanced Algorithms, in which the learning objectives attained are required as prior knowledge.

courseDetails.title: Object-Oriented Programming (for CS)
courseDetails.prerequisites: Students are assumed to have programming skills equivalent to passing the module Programming Fundamentals.

courseDetails.title: Linear Algebra
courseDetails.prerequisites:
The course unit is a prerequisite/entry requirement for following course units:
(1) Introduction to Computer Graphics and Visualization (WBCS056-05)
(2) Introduction to Image Processing (WBCS051-05)
(3) Introduction to Machine Learning (WBCS032-05)

courseDetails.title: Computer Networks
courseDetails.prerequisites:
Assumed prior knowledge:
Introduction to Computing Science (WBCS005-05), Discrete Structures (WBCS011-05), Algorithms and Data Structures in C  (WBCS018 -05).
In particular:
Basic understanding of data structures and algorithms, e.g., graph algorithms like Dijkstra shortest path. Students can write a program in a high-level programming language, e.g., C, JAVA, PYTHON.

courseDetails.title: Advanced Algorithms
courseDetails.prerequisites:
Assumed prior knowledge: the courses Algorithms and Data Structures in C, Discrete Structures, Programming Fundamentals from the degree program Computing Science or equivalent.

More specifically we assume:
 - Knowledge of discrete mathematics (sets, graphs, trees, induction, counting)
 - Ability to program
 - You have implemented basic algorithms and data structures that are taught in the course "Algorithms and Data Structures in C".

courseDetails.title: Advanced Programming
courseDetails.prerequisites:
The course unit assumes prior basic knowledge of the imperative and object-oriented programming paradigms. This means that students are expected to have followed the Programming Fundamentals unit and the Object-Oriented Programming unit, or equivalent. This course unit also assumes knowledge of the Java programming language.

The course unit prepares students for the courses Web Engineering and Software Engineering in the bachelor program Computing Science.

courseDetails.title: Calculus 2
courseDetails.prerequisites: Assumed prior knowledge: Knowledge from 1st-year Calculus 1 (WBCS055-05) and Linear Algebra (WBCS048-05).

courseDetails.title: Functional Programming
courseDetails.prerequisites: This course assumes no prior knowledge, but advises that the student has some programming experience in a regular programming language (like C, Java, Python, Matlab). Moreover, secondary education equivalent to Dutch pre-university education (VWO second phase), is required, including sufficient (discrete) mathematical skills.

courseDetails.title: Web Engineering
courseDetails.prerequisites: The course assumes familiarity with courses Introduction to Information Systems (WBCS021-05), Object-Oriented Programming (WBCS028-05), and Advanced Programming (WBCS053-05) or equivalent.

courseDetails.title: Statistics and Probability
courseDetails.prerequisites: The course assumes prior knowledge acquired from the courses Linear Algebra and Calculus in the BSc of the Computer Science program. Basic programming knowledge is necessary.

courseDetails.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
courseDetails.prerequisites:
Assumed prior knowledge: basic programming skills, knowledge of linear algebra and statistics that are typical of the respective courses included in standard bachelor CS curricula.

This course primarily prepares students for more advanced machine learning courses, such as Introduction to Deep Neural Networks, and for applying machine learning techniques in research projects. It also provides the necessary foundation for MSc-level courses such as Introduction to Data Science, Neural Networks and Computational Intelligence, Pattern Recognition, and related subjects.

courseDetails.title: Software Engineering
courseDetails.prerequisites:
The course unit assumes prior knowledge acquired from the following courses 
* WBCS053-05 Advanced Programming /  WBCS001-05 Advanced Object Oriented Programming 
* WBCS008-05 Web Engineering

courseDetails.title: Operating Systems
courseDetails.prerequisites:
The course unit assumes basic programming experience in a common imperative programming language such as C, C++, Python, or Java. 
The course unit assumes (good) programming experience in C, and some knowledge of C++

courseDetails.title: Languages and Machines
courseDetails.prerequisites: The course assumes prior knowledge acquired from courses Introduction to Logic (CS) (WBCS030-05) and Discrete Structures (WBCS011-05). The course also assumes the maturity of having completed the first year of the BSc Computing Science.

courseDetails.title: Introduction to Computer Graphics and Visualization
courseDetails.prerequisites: Assumed prior knowledge: Calculus 1 (WBCS055-05) and Linear Algebra (WBCS048-05).

courseDetails.title: Research Skills in Computing Science
courseDetails.prerequisites:
The course is meant for students in the final stages of their BSc Computing Science programme. It therefore assumes prior knowledge from many courses from the 1st and 2nd year of the programme, specifically in the area(s) of the topic chosen by the student. 

The course unit is a prerequisite/entry requirement for following course units/degree programmes:
This course aims primarily to train Computing Science students in developing the research skills necessary for the completion of their Bachelor's Project.

courseDetails.title: Information Security
courseDetails.prerequisites: The course unit assumes basic programming experience in a common imperative programming language like C, C++, Python, or Java. It also strongly recommends (not obligatory) a preliminary study of number theory.

courseDetails.title: Fundamentals of Distributed Systems
courseDetails.prerequisites:
Assumed prior knowledge:
Pre-Knowledge on fundamental aspects in computing science obtained for instance in a BSc-Program computing science, in particular:
- Data structures and algorithms, Complexity Analysis
- Basic concepts of Programming Languages
- Basic knowledge on Computer Networks, Computer Architecture or Operating System Principles

courseDetails.title: Bachelor's project
courseDetails.prerequisites:
Completion of all first- year course units
Completion of at least 75 ECTS from years 2 and 3 of the Bachelor Computing Science
Submission of study programme in Progress Portal

components: Algorithms and Data Structures in C (for CS)
Introduction to Computer Graphics and Visualization
progression: The two 60 EC compulsory years have no formal order of examinations. The catalogue places programming, discrete mathematics and core computing before the C algorithms course, and algorithms, linear algebra and calculus before later software, machine learning and visualisation courses. Year-two advanced programming precedes Web Engineering and the second-semester software project.

The 30 EC elective space in semester one is genuine and subject to the published exclusions and approvals. Year three places three 5 EC required courses in block 2a, followed by the 15 EC project in block 2b. The formal project check after block 1b requires all first-year credits, at least 75 EC from years two and three and submission of a study plan. Completion of year two plus a regular 30 EC minor leaves 90 EC by the check. Research Skills is offered in 2a before the project. The older project code mentioned in Research Skills text is not a separate unit.
